ops.title: Session guard: an assignment after cd X && is bound unsure; .orca and heredoc bodies only trip the prefilter
ops.body:
Replay ids 221, 346 and 61 (release-v3 #268 hooks-sweep, replay.md section 4) deny `cd X && B=<literal>; $B ...` and `cd X && CA="<literal>"; "$CA" - <<'Q' ... Q` with "built from text the guard cannot read".

Mechanism, verified by probe on the unmodified hook: `Walk.flush` in bindings.py binds an assignment `Known` only when `sure()` holds, and `sure()` is false when the previous operator is `&&` or `||`. So the assignment after `cd X &&` is `Unknown(source)` and `head_reason` denies the `$B` head. The `.orca/` substring and the heredoc body (which contained the word "Find") only matter for the `names_guarded` prefilter: without a guarded word anywhere on the line the guard never looks, which is why the same assignment with `~/work/x/biome` or with a `hello` heredoc body "allows". Moving the assignment before the `cd` allows.

This is the conditional-assignment rule #243 set on purpose ("deny unresolved command heads built from substitutions or conditional assignments regardless of their source text"); the inline test `cd ~/.claude/worktrees/... && CA="..."; "$CA" ... <<'Q'` -> Block encodes it. Lifting it is a design decision, not a lane fix. Options: (a) bind a top-level `&&`/`||`-chained literal assignment as Known and let the resolved variants be judged, accepting that the prior environment value (reachable only through profile edits, which already defeat the guard via PATH, aliases and functions) is unmodelled; (b) treat `cd DIR &&` specially when DIR resolves to an existing directory at hook time; (c) keep the deny and have the message say to assign before the cd.

PR guard-residuals fixes the other residuals (ids 364, 455, 53) and closes four false negatives found alongside them: the variant re-scan losing `read`-bound names, over-limit variants never scanned, and `caffeinate "$K"` / `find -exec "$K"` with an unresolved target.
